# ataila_audit_events (Data Source)

The platform's audit log: every recorded change, newest first, narrowed by the filters below. The log grows with every change, so a read keeps at most `limit` events (100 when left out); `more` says whether further events matched. The entity before and after each change are left out unless `include_states` is true, which keeps the state small and keeps what the writers recorded (names and addresses among it) out of the state file by default.

Needs `audit-read-global` (or an admin key). A tenant-scoped token reads the events of its own tenant only. Every read is evaluated at plan time: two plans can show different events.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Who changed users in the last week, newest first.
data "ataila_audit_events" "user_changes" {
  action        = "user.*"
  occurred_from = "2026-10-16T00:00:00Z"
  limit         = 200
}

output "user_changes" {
  value = [for e in data.ataila_audit_events.user_changes.events : "${e.occurred_at} ${e.actor} ${e.action} ${e.entity_id}"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `action` (String) Exact action, or a prefix when it ends in `*` (`user.*`).
- `actor` (String) Exact actor: a person's e-mail address (compared lower-cased), `system` or `pipeline:<run id>`.
- `auth_kind` (String) How the actor authenticated: `session`, `pat`, `service_account` or `ci`.
- `entity_id` (String) Exact entity id, as the writer spelled it.
- `entity_type` (String) Exact entity type, e.g. `users`.
- `include_states` (Boolean) Also keep each event's `before_state` and `after_state` (JSON); false when left out.
- `limit` (Number) The most events to keep, newest first: 1-1000; 100 when left out.
- `occurred_from` (String) Events at or after this time (RFC 3339).
- `occurred_to` (String) Events before this time (RFC 3339, exclusive).
- `request_id` (String) Events of one request (`X-Request-ID`).
- `tenant_id` (String) Events attributed to this tenant.
- `token_id` (String) Events made with this API token (its id).

### Read-Only

- `events` (Attributes List) The matching events, newest first. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--events))
- `more` (Boolean) True when more events matched than `limit` kept.

<a id="nestedatt--events"></a>
### Nested Schema for `events`

Read-Only:

- `action` (String) What was done, e.g. `user.create`.
- `actor` (String) Who made the change: an e-mail address as it was then, `system` or `pipeline:<run id>`.
- `after_state` (String) The entity after the change, as JSON; null unless `include_states` (and on a delete).
- `auth_kind` (String) `session`, `pat`, `service_account` or `ci`; null when not recorded.
- `before_state` (String) The entity before the change, as JSON; null unless `include_states` (and on a create).
- `entity_id` (String) Which one, as the writer spelled its id; null when none was recorded.
- `entity_type` (String) The kind of thing changed.
- `id` (String) The event's id: a positive integer as a string.
- `occurred_at` (String) When the change was recorded (RFC 3339, UTC).
- `request_id` (String) The request's `X-Request-ID`, when recorded.
- `source_ip` (String) The client address as the platform saw it, when recorded.
- `tenant_id` (String) The tenant the event is attributed to, when its writer recorded one.
- `token_id` (String) The API token used, for `pat` and `service_account`.
